reviews.review: it's a classic and incredibly cheap, give it a whirl with some friends for a good time. more content than risk of rain 2.

Love this game.  Side-scrolling sci-fi Binding of Isaac (truly, Risk of Rain deserves the honor of that comparison), with an interesting new mechanic - really the defining feature - which is simply the timer: every few minutes, the difficulty increases.  You can see the timer and the current difficulty at all times, so it lends a strong sense of urgency that creates interesting choices - you've found the exit, but know there's a big unexplored section that may house many chests full of new powers.... do I go for it?  A disciplined player probably wouldn't, but me... I want to experience THE POWER!  

The replayability is enormous: each play feels different (at least once you get 5-10 minutes in) because the number of items you can find is so vast, and they combine in interesting ways.  On top of that, as you make various achievements, other playable characters and new items become available for future plays.  Each character is very very different.

PS: Many games label themselves roguelike, rogue-lite, whatever, but few truly feel roguish... Risk of Rain is roguish to the core!  It takes the formula of perm-death, difficulty, a vast array of powers and equipment that combine in interesting ways drastically changing your play-style throughout each run...

This game is 10/10. Such a fantastic Rogue-Like with a great flavor and style that let me grind away 100+ hours easily into this game. I 100% completed the game, all achieves, all items, monster logs ect.

I look forward to Risk of Rain 2

A great game for playing while listening to podcasts, and probably the best roguelike I've played. It has a perfect amount of variation, with every playthrough feeling familiar, but still being different enough to be exciting. It's also simple enough that you barely need to think while playing it, which is a great thing for when listening to podcasts.
